main.title: Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney
main.subtitle: Two investigators enter Labyrinthia
main.summary: Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney brings Level-5's puzzle-solving professor and Capcom's defence lawyer into a shared Nintendo 3DS adventure. Their paths meet in Labyrinthia, a town where witch trials and a mysterious Storyteller govern everyday life. Layton and Luke investigate its apparent impossibilities while Phoenix and Maya face accusations in court. The crossover divides its work between exploring a strange place and defending the people caught inside its rules, allowing the two series to approach the same mystery with their own methods.

cards.heading: Two investigators enter Labyrinthia
cards.text: Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney brings Level-5's puzzle-solving professor and Capcom's defence lawyer into a shared Nintendo 3DS adventure. Their paths meet in Labyrinthia, a town where witch trials and a mysterious Storyteller govern everyday life. Layton and Luke investigate its apparent impossibilities while Phoenix and Maya face accusations in court. The crossover divides its work between exploring a strange place and defending the people caught inside its rules, allowing the two series to approach the same mystery with their own methods.

cards.heading: A puzzle can prepare a defence
cards.text: Adventure sections use a movable magnifying glass to inspect the town, find hint coins and start conversations. Characters present puzzles whose solutions earn Picarats, preserving Layton's familiar pattern of small intellectual diversions inside a larger investigation. The witch trials then ask Phoenix to examine testimony and present evidence against contradictions. The change of setting gives those courtroom rules unusual material: claims of magic must be tested through details that can actually be observed. Information gathered outside court becomes useful when a confident explanation fails under questioning.

cards.heading: Several witnesses share the stand
cards.text: The trials allow groups of witnesses to testify together. While one speaks, another may react, giving Phoenix an opportunity to question the reaction and uncover a new connection. Comparing the people on the stand becomes as important as comparing a statement with an item in the record. The arrangement suits a story about collective belief and public accusation. Animated sequences and voiced scenes bring the visiting casts together, while the investigations and hearings keep their different strengths recognisable throughout the journey through Labyrinthia.

main.title: Far Cry 3
main.subtitle: Survival and Vaas on the Rook Islands
main.summary: Far Cry 3 is a 2012 first-person shooter game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft.

cards.heading: Jason Brody’s escape across the Rook Islands
cards.text: Far Cry 3 is a 2012 first-person shooter game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft. It is the third main installment in the Far Cry series after Far Cry 2. The game takes place on the fictional Rook Islands, a tropical archipelago which can be freely explored by players. Gameplay focuses on combat and exploration. Players can use a variety of weapons to defeat human enemies and hostile wildlife, and the game features elements found in role-playing games such as skill trees and experience. After a vacation goes awry, protagonist Jason Brody must save his friends, who have been kidnapped by pirates, and escape from the island and its unhinged inhabitants.

cards.heading: Designing an island and creating Vaas
cards.text: Ubisoft Montreal collaborated with Ubisoft's global development team, including Massive Entertainment, Ubisoft Shanghai, Ubisoft Bucharest, Ubisoft Reflections and Red Storm Entertainment. The game's development was partially restarted in 2010 after the departure of several key creative staff. The team evaluated the feedback for Far Cry 2 and identified areas that needed to be improved or removed. The team spent considerable time designing the island, which they described as the "second most important character" in the game. Inspirations were taken from films and TV shows such as Apocalypse Now and Lost, as well as video games The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim and Red Dead Redemption. Michael Mando was hired to portray Vaas Montenegro, an antagonist the team compared to Darth Vader. The game was announced in June 2011 and Ubisoft promoted the game with various companion apps, webseries and crossover.

cards.heading: Acclaim, ten million sales and a lasting legacy
cards.text: Far Cry 3 reached Windows, PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in November 2012. Critics praised Vaas, the world design, progression and combat, while the multiplayer modes drew criticism. Sales reached ten million copies. Ubisoft followed with the standalone Blood Dragon in 2013 and Far Cry 4 in 2014, with later ports returning players to the Rook Islands.

main.title: Yakuza 5
main.subtitle: Five playable protagonists in Yakuza's fifth main chapter
main.summary: Yakuza 5 is a 2012 action-adventure game developed by Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio and published by Sega for the PlayStation 3.

cards.heading: A PlayStation 3 debut before later remasters
cards.text: Yakuza 5 is a 2012 action-adventure game developed by Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio and published by Sega for the PlayStation 3. It is the fifth main entry in the Yakuza series. The game was released in December 2012 in Japan, and localized for North America, Europe and Australia as a PlayStation Network download in December 2015. A remaster with improved resolution and frame rate was released for the PlayStation 4 on June 20, 2019, in Japan, and worldwide on February 11, 2020, as part of The Yakuza Remastered Collection. Versions for Windows and Xbox One were released in January 2021.

cards.heading: City exploration, arcade games and faster combat
cards.text: Players explore larger city areas, take part in side activities and enter fights during the adventure. Arcade games include Virtua Fighter 2 and Taiko No Tatsujin. Transitions into combat are smoother than before, keeping encounters connected to movement through the city.

cards.heading: Five protagonists, including Haruka's rhythm story
cards.text: Five protagonists share the story: Kazuma Kiryu, Shun Akiyama and Taiga Saejima return, joined by Tatsuo Shinada and Haruka Sawamura. Haruka becomes playable for the first time, with rhythm-based activities replacing the fighting used by the others. Her progress still incorporates familiar systems such as a Heat gauge.

main.title: Fantasy Life
main.subtitle: A profession can change the journey
main.summary: On December 27, 2012, LEVEL-5 released Fantasy Life in Japan for Nintendo 3DS, in both physical and digital form.

cards.heading: Choosing a Life in Reveria
cards.text: LEVEL-5 released Fantasy Life for Nintendo 3DS in Japan on December 27, 2012. Twelve professions, called Lives, connect combat, gathering and crafting across Reveria. A player can change profession while keeping useful skills, turning a mined material into a crafted item and then equipment for another role.

cards.heading: Twelve linked professions
cards.text: Lives support one another. A Miner extracts metal, a Blacksmith makes a weapon and a combat profession uses it in the field. Changing Life opens another set of tasks and abilities within the same world. The character gradually gains practical experience across several professions.

cards.heading: From gathered material to crafted item
cards.text: Crafting gives gathered materials further uses. Ore can become a tool, wood can supply furnishings and exploration can uncover resources for the next project. Improving one profession therefore benefits another, giving activities such as fishing or cutting wood a place in wider progression.

cards.heading: A home between adventures
cards.text: Players can buy homes in different towns and decorate them with furniture they make. The journey alternates between dangerous areas, gathering trips and quieter domestic activities. Nobuo Uematsu's music and Yoshitaka Amano's illustrative artwork contribute to the bright fantasy setting.

main.title: Kentucky Route Zero
main.subtitle: Conway makes a final delivery along a mysterious road
main.summary: Kentucky Route Zero is a 2013–2020 point-and-click adventure interactive fiction game developed by Cardboard Computer and published by Annapurna Interactive.

cards.heading: Conway and the people along Route Zero
cards.text: Kentucky Route Zero is a 2013–2020 point-and-click adventure interactive fiction game developed by Cardboard Computer and published by Annapurna Interactive. The game follows the narrative of a truck driver named Conway and the strange people he meets as he tries to cross the mysterious Route Zero in Kentucky to make a final delivery for the antiques company he works for.

cards.heading: Acclaim for visual art and storytelling
cards.text: The game received acclaim for its visual art, narrative, characterization, atmosphere, and themes, appearing on several best-of-the-decade lists.

cards.heading: Five acts released from 2013 to 2020
cards.text: Kentucky Route Zero was first revealed in 2011 via the crowdfunding platform Kickstarter and is separated into five acts that were released sporadically throughout its development; the first releasing in January 2013 and the last releasing in January 2020. The game was developed for Linux, Windows, and macOS, with console ports for the Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One under the subtitle of "TV Edition", coinciding with the release of the final act. The game was released for Android and iOS on December 13, 2022, in partnership with Netflix and was later released for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S in August 2023.

main.title: DmC: Devil May Cry
main.subtitle: Dante enters a changing Limbo
main.summary: DmC: Devil May Cry is Ninja Theory?s reinterpretation of Capcom?s action series, with a younger Dante and a city that changes around him.

cards.heading: A new Dante in Limbo
cards.text: DmC: Devil May Cry is a 2013 action game developed by Ninja Theory for Capcom. Its younger Dante fights through Limbo, a distorted contemporary city. Combos, style ratings and rapid weapon switching remain central, while Angel and Demon powers add new ways to attack and cross the environment.

cards.heading: Reinterpreting the series
cards.text: Capcom asked Ninja Theory to reinterpret the series for a contemporary setting. Dante?s appearance and identity changed, but the combat retained enemy launchers, combinations of weapons and ratings that rewarded stylish play. Players could recognise familiar techniques beneath the new presentation.

cards.heading: Angel and Demon modifiers
cards.text: Holding the Angel or Demon modifier changes Dante?s weapons and abilities during a combo. Angel tools are fast and useful against groups, while Demon weapons hit harder. The same distinction extends to traversal: Dante can pull himself towards a target or drag objects towards him.

cards.heading: A city that changes around Dante
cards.text: Limbo?s streets, walls and signs deform as Dante passes. Buildings close around him, passages narrow and messages appear across the scenery. Ninja Theory used Unreal Engine 3 with custom lighting, materials and effects to create the colourful, shifting city. Its architecture becomes another obstacle to evade while fighting.

main.title: Dead Space 3
main.subtitle: Isaac and Carver face the frozen world of Tau Volantis
main.summary: Visceral Games sends Isaac Clarke to Tau Volantis to investigate the Necromorph threat. Customizable weapons and online cooperation with John Carver bring new systems to the third main Dead Space.

cards.heading: A frozen planet and the origins of the Necromorphs
cards.text: Dead Space 3 is a 2013 survival horror action video game developed by Visceral Games and published by Electronic Arts for PlayStation 3, Windows, and Xbox 360. It is the third and final main entry in the Dead Space series. The game's story follows player-character Isaac Clarke and his allies as they explore a frozen planet, Tau Volantis, to discover the origins of the growing threat from their enemies, the Necromorphs. Players control Isaac and explore the environment, solve puzzles, and find resources, while fighting Necromorphs and hostile humans called Unitologists. The game supports online cooperative multiplayer sessions in which a second player takes the role of new character John Carver.

cards.heading: Crafting weapons to dismember the enemy
cards.text: Isaac must fight several types of Necromorphs that emerge from the environment; he also encounters human enemies, and occasional three-way battles between Isaac, Necromorphs, and human soldiers occur. Isaac can use two weapons to combat the Necromorphs, which can only be killed by severing their limbs, a method called strategic dismemberment. In addition to standard movement-based combat, Isaac can move into cover behind some objects such as box piles. All weapons draw from a pool of universal ammunition. Some items such as health, weapons, and ammunition can be found in the environment, and additional items and customized weapons are created using crafting benches that are found during the campaign. Weapons are crafted using blueprints and can be customized with multiple firing types, melee counter enhancements, and buffs to enhance damage. Crafting resources are found in the environment; these are retrieved using a scavenger robot and are collected with ammunition from defeated enemies. Resources can also be purchased with real money in microtransactions using the bench interface.

cards.heading: John Carver and asymmetrical hallucinations
cards.text: A second player joins as John Carver, bringing cooperative side missions and scenes into the campaign. Some sequences give the partners different hallucinations, so describing what each can see becomes part of staying together. The Xbox 360 version also accepts Kinect voice commands for actions such as stasis. Finishing the game unlocks ways to approach it again: New Game Plus carries equipment forward, Classic removes crafting, Pure Survival makes resource management central, and Hardcore limits the player to one life. These modes change how much security the same supplies and encounters can offer.

main.title: Sly Cooper: Thieves in Time
main.subtitle: A time-travelling heist to save the Cooper family history
main.summary: Sanzaru Games reunites Sly and his gang to restore the Thievius Raccoonus. The original PlayStation 3 and PS Vita adventure links time-travelling heists with Cross-Buy and cloud saves.

cards.heading: The Cooper family history begins to disappear
cards.text: Sly Cooper: Thieves in Time sends the raccoon thief and his gang through the history of his family. The pages of the Thievius Raccoonus are changing, and repairing the book requires discovering who is interfering with the Cooper line. Sanzaru Games developed this fourth adventure after remastering the original trilogy, with Sony publishing it for PlayStation 3 and Vita in 2013. Sly, Bentley, Murray and Carmelita share the journey with Sly's ancestors. Their different skills turn each period into another set of routes, disguises and tasks needed to carry out a heist.

cards.heading: Hidden treasures, clue bottles and a Vita view
cards.text: New secret masks and treasures are hidden throughout the game; the latter item, unlike its counterpart in previous installments, is collectible only and cannot be sold on the game's ThiefNet service (although the player still receives an in-game monetary reward). The clue bottles from Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus and Sly 2: Band of Thieves make a return, allowing the player to unlock new abilities for all of the playable characters. A new feature allows anyone who owns both the PlayStation Vita and PlayStation 3 versions of the game to use the Vita system as "a set of x-ray goggles" to find any of these hidden collectibles anywhere in the world, through the use of augmented reality. The binary characters displayed during Bentley's plans are ASCII-encoded text messages and can be decoded manually.

cards.heading: Cross-Buy connects the console and handheld editions
cards.text: Sly Cooper: Thieves in Time was a part of Sony's cross-buy initiative, allowing purchasers of the PlayStation 3 version of the game to receive a free copy of the game for the PlayStation Vita via the PlayStation Network. However, the PlayStation Vita version was not part of the scheme, meaning that it did not include a free copy of the PlayStation 3 version. The player can also save their game in the cloud, allowing them to play on one system and later continue playing on the other.

main.title: Crysis 3
main.subtitle: Prophet hunts through an overgrown New York
main.summary: Crytek combines the ruined city with a returning jungle as Prophet confronts the Alpha Ceph. The Nanosuit, a compound bow and the asymmetrical Hunter mode expand the original 2013 shooter.

cards.heading: A city reclaimed by jungle and the Seven Wonders
cards.text: Crysis 3 returns Prophet to a post-apocalyptic New York where vegetation has overtaken the city. Crytek's 2013 shooter combines the urban setting of Crysis 2 with the open terrain of the original, giving each area different cover and routes. Prophet hunts the Alpha Ceph while relying on a Nanosuit that can conceal or protect him. A compound bow and the ability to hack hostile equipment expand those choices. Developed over twenty-three months, with multiplayer by Crytek UK, the game concludes the trilogy through a landscape designed to allow more freedom than its predecessor.

cards.heading: Cloaking, the bow and hacked enemy technology
cards.text: The Nanosuit lets Prophet approach a group unseen or absorb damage in a slower armour mode. His bow can fire without breaking the cloak, and spent arrows can be recovered. Other firearms expose him until the camouflage cools down. Hacking offers another approach: mines, turrets, drones and security systems can become weapons against their owners. Attachments and ammunition alter how equipment works, including explosive or electric arrows. Upgrade modules found in the world improve the suit's properties and abilities. Choosing a route therefore includes deciding which protection, weapon or captured device will support it.

cards.heading: Hunters turn defeated CELL soldiers into pursuers
cards.text: In addition to traditional multiplayer modes, a new multiplayer mode, the Hunter mode, is featured in the game. It is an asymmetrical multiplayer mode which pits two teams of players, playing as either hunters, or troopers from CELL, against each other. The three CELL classes are equipped with completely different weapons, and defeated troopers respawn as hunters and have to defeat their former teammates. Hunters are equipped with the nanosuit and infinite cloak, as well as the Hunter Bow, which allows the hunter to fire while they're cloaked. The hunters also have access to a Thermite Arrow tip, and the CELL have various explosives and weapons that change depending on class selected. The PC version of the game can accommodate up to 16 players, while the console versions can only support 12 players.

main.title: Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance
main.subtitle: Raiden takes Metal Gear into action combat
main.summary: Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance takes Raiden into a direct action game developed by PlatinumGames with Kojima Productions.

cards.heading: A new job for Raiden
cards.text: Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance takes Raiden into a direct action game developed by PlatinumGames with Kojima Productions. Released in 2013, it follows the cyborg swordsman in a world where private military companies employ advanced combat technology. The familiar Metal Gear setting now supports a different kind of confrontation.

cards.heading: Choose the cut
cards.text: Blade Mode lets the player aim the direction of Raiden's sword rather than simply watch a fixed finishing animation. A carefully placed strike can expose an enemy's energy source for Zandatsu. Cutting becomes both a visible effect and a way to recover the resources needed to keep fighting.

cards.heading: A changed place in the story
cards.text: PlatinumGames records that the project began as Metal Gear Solid: Rising, intended to bridge earlier appearances of Raiden. When the collaboration changed, the setting moved to several years after Metal Gear Solid 4. The finished game therefore reflects a production change in its story as well as in its combat.
